title: Academy run-and-sort
materials: Three wall signs: each academy’s name, founding year, location and branch
Room to run between the walls

displayContent.headline: Which academy?
displayContent.body: Listen to the name. Run to the wall of the academy you think he graduated from. Your patrol scores when most of you pick right.
points: Colorado Springs: U.S. Air Force Academy

prompts.answer: Air Force Academy, class of 1965: its first graduate to receive the Medal of Honor
Air Force Academy, class of 1973: the pilot who landed his airliner on the Hudson River
West Point (Army), class of 1951. The Army’s academy produced the second man on the Moon.
Air Force Academy, class of 1970. The Air Force’s academy produced a famous NBA coach.

prompts.text: Bonus point: name the other two federal service academies.
prompts.answer: The Coast Guard Academy in New London, Connecticut, and the Merchant Marine Academy in Kings Point, New York.

leaderScript: Before the meeting, post the three wall signs.
Press → to show each name. Boys run to a wall; a patrol scores when most of its members picked right.
Press R to show the answer, then → for the next name.
Aldrin and Popovich come last on purpose: a moonwalker from the Army’s academy and an NBA coach from the Air Force’s make good arguments.
Finish with the bonus question, then the answer key.

discussionQuestions.question: Why would the Naval Academy commission Marines as well as Navy officers?
discussionQuestions.answer: The Marine Corps is part of the Department of the Navy.

ifShortOnTime: Read six names: Grant, Nimitz, Sijan, Lee, then Aldrin and Popovich. Skip the bonus.
lowVolunteerNote: With two leaders, run this and the floor calendar as side-by-side stations and swap patrols at 0:40.
